summary:
2026-10-17 (overnight release push): Caught a real shipped-build bug while prepping the winget submission: windows-v0.1.4 was built from a pre-"CEF Linux-only" commit (Cargo.toml had `default = ["cef"]` for every target), so it bundled the full Chromium/CEF runtime on Windows and crashed on launch (ICU data file descriptor error) - confirmed live by installing+running it on the owner's real Windows box over Tailscale SSH. Current main's Cargo.toml already scopes `cef` to Linux-only (from the public-release prep), but no Windows build had been cut since - so this was a real regression nobody had caught, not a new decision. Fixed by committing scripts/build-windows-cross.sh (existed only as a loose file in an old worktree, referenced by docs but never actually committed) and cutting a real wry/WebView2 build: ~15MB installed vs 325MB+, confirmed via the same live Windows box (install, ARP entry, WebView2 runtime detection all checked) before the box got busy with the owner's own concurrent work there - full runtime/WebRTC verification on real hardware is still open, see needs. Bumped the whole app to 0.1.5 (Cargo.toml/tauri.conf.json/package.json x3/android build.gradle/iOS MARKETING_VERSION) and used the existing ~/jor-release tooling (release-linux.sh --windows-fallback) to build both platforms from a clean worktree and publish as Forgejo prereleases (linux-v0.1.5, windows-v0.1.5) - then PUBLISHED them (not left as drafts), since the owner explicitly asked for these to be live tonight. Also: rebuilt+published Android (android-v0.1.5, real upload-key-signed APK+AAB, JDK21 env fix for the known gradle gotcha) and triggered the real Codemagic ios-release workflow via a tag push (ios-v0.1.12) - it built, signed, and published a real IPA to TestFlight the same night (no public invite link generated yet). Built two new self-hosted distribution channels from scratch, both verified end-to-end, not just assembled: a GPG-signed apt repo (reprepro in a throwaway container + manual signing with the existing releases@jorkonvo.com key; verified with a real `apt install` in a fresh debian:bookworm container) and a self-hosted F-Droid repo via fdroidserver (not eligible for the main f-droid.org index - the app links Firebase Cloud Messaging for push, which the official index disallows regardless of license). Both are gitignored where they hold secrets/regenerable binaries (site/apt/dists+pool, site/fdroid/ entirely - its config.yml has the repo keystore password in plaintext) - only jorkonvo.gpg/.asc (the public key) is tracked. Prepped but did NOT submit (each needs a human-held third-party account or a final look, same judgment call as the Flathub PR earlier): a Chocolatey package (packaging/windows/choco, syntax-checked only - no Linux choco client to test-pack with), the winget manifest (bumped to point at the fixed 0.1.5 build on the existing fork branch, replacing one that pointed at the broken 0.1.4), and the AUR jorkonvo-bin PKGBUILD (bumped + verified with a real `makepkg -si` in an Arch container - genuinely installs; still blocked on registering an aur.archlinux.org account, a dedicated SSH keypair is generated and ready at ~/.ssh/aur_jorkonvo). Rewrote site/index.html's download section: real copy-paste apt/AUR commands, the F-Droid repo URL, the Android APK link, iOS TestFlight status - and corrected a stale note claiming the repo was still private (it's been public for a while, verified live). Also discovered the repo visibility blocker noted below was already stale/resolved.

Windows code-signing via SignPath.io's free OSS program hit a real wall: it requires a 'Reputation' showing the project is already trusted/used, which a brand-new project can't show without fabricating evidence - owner explicitly said not to fake it and to defer Windows signing. A public GitHub mirror (github.com/thatumi/JorKonvo) exists as a byproduct and stays public on purpose for discoverability. (2) Designed an original app logo (chat bubble + equalizer bars, violet gradient - replacing a generic-looking placeholder, discovered the splash screens were also unbranded placeholders and fixed those too) and rolled it out everywhere: desktop/web/Android/iOS icons, Play Store graphics. Rebuilt and republished Linux (published) and Windows (published) 0.1.4 with the new icon baked in end-to-end (GPG re-signed); rebuilt the Android AAB (handed off for manual Play Console upload). Found+fixed a real missed bug along the way: AUR packaging (jorkonvo-bin) still said license=custom:proprietary after the earlier MIT relicensing - fixed. (3) Flathub: the existing Flatpak manifest only repackages a prebuilt .deb, which Flathub doesn't allow. Built a genuine from-source manifest (packaging/linux/flatpak-flathub/) - the hard part was CEF (Chromium Embedded Framework): reverse-engineered cef-dll-sys's build.rs directly from its crates.io source to find the CEF_PATH vendoring mechanism (the documented dev.crabnebula.Platform Flatpak runtime doesn't actually exist on Flathub - verified and reported honestly before pivoting), vendored CEF's prebuilt binaries as a pinned+checksummed source (same pattern Electron apps use on Flathub, not a policy violation), and discovered Linux's cef feature doesn't need cmake/ninja at all (only windows/macos do) - it just links libcef.so directly and copies runtime files next to the binary (confirmed RUNPATH=$ORIGIN on the real binary), so the manifest skips Tauri's whole AppImage/deb bundler and just assembles /app/lib/jorkonvo/ directly. Generated offline npm/cargo vendoring via flatpak-node-generator/flatpak-cargo-generator. Verified end-to-end TWICE with the Flathub-matched builder (flatpak run org.flatpak.Builder, not just the older apt flatpak-builder 1.2.3 which hit an appstream-compose/appstreamcli naming mismatch against GNOME Sdk 51 - a local tooling-version issue, not a manifest bug): once with local sources for fast iteration, once with the actual submission-shape sources (git clone of github.com/thatumi/JorKonvo @ 8764ea4, real cef-builds.spotifycdn.com URL) - both built, appstreamcli-composed, and exported cleanly, and the exported app installs and launches (CEF initializes; the only errors seen under Xvfb - no system dbus, no EGL/GPU - are headless-test-host limitations, not packaging defects). AUR publishing itself still blocked on a genuinely owner-only step: no AUR account/SSH key exists yet. | 2026-10-09 (later): Linux speaker/mic device list FIXED and verified live - strings on libcef.so showed Chromium has a full PulseAudio backend compiled in and prefers it for per-device enumeration, falling back to ALSA's one generic device when libpulse.so.0 isn't dlopen-able (the live symptom: owner only saw 'Default'/'System Default'). scripts/build-linux.sh gained pulse_prepare/pulse_copy_into (same pinned-Debian-12-pool pattern as the existing PipeWire fix) bundling libpulse0 + its full transitive chain (libsndfile and its FLAC/vorbis/opus/ogg/mpg123/lame codec deps, libsystemd, libasyncns and their own deps - 18 packages, since the loader resolves every NEEDED entry at dlopen() time regardless of whether it's ever called) so the client library can reach pipewire-pulse's PulseAudio-compatible socket, present on virtually every modern desktop.
